newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain seen holding rate on Tuesday - poll.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain seen holding rate on Tuesday - poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is likely to keep its key money rate unchanged at 6.75 percent on Tuesday at its regular repo auction, but is expected to cut it by 25 basis points before year end, according to a Reuter poll.
All 10 financial analysts surveyed on Monday said the central bank would likely await November inflation data, due on December 13, before sanctioning its seventh reduction in the year.

Although November inflation data would be announced by the National Statistics Institute INE only after the Bank of Spain's repo results, dealers said the Bank of Spain may be informed on the inflation data beforehand.
October inflation, which rose a modest 0.1 percent monthly and 3.5 percent yearly, boosted the market's expectations of a fresh rate cut before year-end.
If November inflation moderates further, analysts said that might give the Bank of Spain justification for a further cut.
On October 3, the Bank of Spain made its sixth interest rate reduction, cutting the key rate 50 basis points to 6.75 percent.
The rate started the year at nine percent.
